findings.title: The process type check prevents hung spawned workers from being killed
findings.body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so this check is false for every production worker. When a worker hangs, the manager starts its replacement without killing the original. Repeated restarts leak child processes, and an original worker that resumes can flush concurrently with its replacement. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish processes from test threads. The same incorrect check also prevents termination in join().

findings.title: Do not skip worker cleanup when the join deadline expires
findings.body: The deadline check breaks out of the entire worker loop. If next_step.join() consumes the timeout, no workers are cleaned up; if the first worker consumes it, all remaining workers are skipped. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown and cannot stop a worker blocked in Redis or a Kafka delivery future. Such workers survive join() and can accumulate across rebalances. Regardless of the waiting deadline, perform termination cleanup for every worker.

findings.title: The added flusher synchronization sleep is patched into a no-op
findings.body: This test replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, which also replaces this newly added time.sleep(0.1) call. Consequently, it does not wait for the background flusher to observe the drift change or produce a message. step.join() then sets the flusher's stopped flag, so the expected message can be missed depending on thread scheduling. Synchronize on production of the expected message using an event or another unpatched waiting mechanism before shutting down the flusher.
